as="geometry"/></mxCell><mxCell id="c126" value="<b style="font-size:14px">How clients stay apart in a shared cell</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#5b6675">1. Data, keys and models are separate Azure resources per client, in the client&#x27;s own resource group.<br>2. Each client has its own identities. Only id-&lt;client&gt;-app can use the client&#x27;s storage, vault and index;<br> only id-&lt;client&gt;-gw can call the client&#x27;s Azure OpenAI. Keys are off everywhere, so a token is the only way in.<br>3. The gateway API for a client accepts only that client&#x27;s app token and calls out only as that client&#x27;s gateway identity.<br>4. Container apps accept traffic only from the App Gateway subnet, so one client&#x27;s app can&#x27;t call another&#x27;s.<br>5. Per-client deployment identity: Contributor on its own resource group only. The cell identity has no data roles.<br>6. svg.text: Tier 2: shared cell. Shared front door, compute and AI gateway; every client keeps its own data, keys, models and identities

ADR 0014. One subscription (a 'cell') holds up to 20 clients. What's shared processes client traffic but stores none of it; everything that stores client data is per client and only that client's identities can use it.
northwind's ranges to the cell App
Each client app trusts only its own
a B2B group). A user who reaches
another client's host name gets a
All clients share one frontend IP, so
the hub firewall and Private Link can't
tell clients apart by address. The host
name, per-site WAF rules and sign-in
groups, scoped to the client RG
sub: aiadv-cell-eus2-01 (terraform/stamps/cell + one terraform/stamps/cell-client per client)
Vended once by P&T into the AI Advisory / Clients MG. A full cell gets a sibling: aiadv-cell-eus2-02.
rg-cell01-prd-eus2 (shared: carries client traffic, stores no client data)
vnet-cell01-prd-eus2 (10.110.0.0/22), peered to the hub; 0.0.0.0/0 -> hub firewall
one listener, TLS certificate and WAF policy per client
host name picks the client's backend; require SNI
per-site WAF: client IP allow-list + rate limit
Private Link frontend for clients on Azure
access + WAF logs to the cell workspace, no bodies
accepts only that client's id-<client>-app token
calls that client's Azure OpenAI as id-<client>-gw
token limit + token metric per client (showback)
prompt and response bodies never logged
Each client's endpoints point only at that client's resources. Reaching an endpoint's IP is not access:
keys are off everywhere, and only Entra tokens for the client's own identities are accepted.
one index per client, push only
Deployed by id-deploy-cell01 (shared RG + per-client wiring). It holds no role on any client's data.
per client: client data, keys, models; deployed by id-deploy-northwind
gw: OpenAI User on own AOAI
per client: client data, keys, models; deployed by id-deploy-tailspin
Azure OpenAI · Storage · Key Vault · Log Analytics
same shape as northwind; only tailspin's identities have roles
per client: client data, keys, models; deployed by id-deploy-litware
Azure OpenAI · Storage · Key Vault · Log Analytics
same shape as northwind; only litware's identities have roles
Adding a client = a new client RG + one entry
in the cell's clients map. No vending, no new
How clients stay apart in a shared cell
1. Data, keys and models are separate Azure resources per client, in the client's own resource group.
2. Each client has its own identities. Only id-<client>-app can use the client's storage, vault and index;
only id-<client>-gw can call the client's Azure OpenAI. Keys are off everywhere, so a token is the only way in.
3. The gateway API for a client accepts only that client's app token and calls out only as that client's gateway identity.
4. Container apps accept traffic only from the App Gateway subnet, so one client's app can't call another's.
5. Per-client deployment identity: Contributor on its own resource group only. The cell identity has no data roles.
6. Terraform tests assert 1 to 5 for every client in the cell's clients map.
What it costs (approx. list price, USD/month)
Shared per cell: App Gateway WAF_v2 ~400, APIM ~700 (Standard v2*), AI Search S1 x2 ~490,
Container Apps environment ~0 idle, cell Log Analytics ~50. About 1,650 per cell.
Per client: 3 private endpoints ~22, logs ~25, an always-on replica ~40, tokens as used.
About 90 per client + 1,650 / clients in the cell. At 20 clients: ~170 per client.
*Premium APIM (internal VNet mode, as built today) is ~2,800: ~280 per client at 20.
Tier 1 is ~700 to ~1,400 per client before tokens (~3,500 with a Premium gateway).
Fits: confidential client data where the contract accepts shared, Microsoft-managed
compute and edge, but wants dedicated data stores, keys, models and logs. Most hosted
solutions. Onboarding in hours, not days: no vending, no new gateway.
Doesn't fit: contracts that require a dedicated subscription, network-level separation,
their own ExpressRoute path with per-client firewall rules, or PTU capacity of their own.
Those clients stay on Tier 1. Moving up is a data copy plus a new stamp.
Shared in the cell: carries client traffic, stores none
Per client: client data, keys, models, identities
User path: client network -> hub firewall -> shared App Gateway (listener per client) -> client's app
Model path: client's app -> shared AI gateway (client's API) -> client's own Azure OpenAI
Data path: client's app identity -> its own storage, vault and search index (private endpoints)
Egress: cell workload subnets -> hub firewall (UDR)
Private Link: client's own Azure VNet -> private endpoint -> cell App Gateway Private Link
Sources: docs/adr/0014-isolation-tiers.md, docs/architecture/isolation-tiers.md, terraform/stamps/cell, terraform/stamps/cell-client. Names and addresses are the example configs.
